### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and efficiency. | # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |---|------------|----------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office work) and how much you’re willing to spend. | Use online PC builders (e.g., PCPartPicker) to compare prices and check compatibility. | | 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | A clean, static‑free area and the right tools prevent damage. | • Phillips screwdriver (magnetic head)
• Anti‑static wrist strap (optional but recommended)
• Small container for screws
• Clean, flat table or desk | | 3 | **Choose a Case** | Determines airflow, size, and aesthetics. | • ATX mid‑tower for most builds
• Mini‑ITX for compact builds
• Look for good cable management and dust filters | | 4 | **Select a Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components; must be reliable. | • 80+ Gold or better for efficiency
• Wattage: 500W–750W for mid‑range, 850W+ for high‑end or overclocking
• Modular cables reduce clutter | | 5 | **Pick a Motherboard** | Hosts CPU, RAM, storage, expansion slots. | • Match socket type to CPU (e.g., LGA 1200, AM4, LGA 1700)
• Check BIOS version (some boards need updates for newer CPUs)
• Ensure enough PCIe slots, M.2 slots, USB ports | | 6 | **Choose a CPU** | Core performance, clock speed, integrated graphics. | • Intel Core i5/i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 5/7/9
• Consider integrated GPU if you won’t buy a discrete GPU | | 7 | **Get RAM** | Speed and capacity affect multitasking and gaming. | • DDR4 or DDR5 depending on motherboard
• 16GB is a solid baseline; 32GB for heavy workloads | | 8 | **Select Storage** | SSDs are faster; HDDs add bulk. | • NVMe M.2 SSD for OS + games (250GB–1TB)
• SATA SSD/HDD for bulk storage | | 9 | **Pick a Graphics Card (GPU)** | Essential for gaming, video editing, AI tasks. | • NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070/3080 or AMD Radeon RX 6700/6800/6900
• Match GPU size to case clearance | | 10 | **Add Cooling** | Keeps components within safe temperatures. | • Stock cooler (often comes with CPU)
• Aftermarket air cooler or AIO liquid cooler for higher performance
• Ensure case fans support airflow direction | | 11 | **Check Compatibility** | Avoid dead components. | • Use PCPartPicker’s “Compatibility” tab
• Verify dimensions (GPU length, PSU length, cooler height) | | 12 | **Prepare the Case** | Remove panels, install standoffs, set up PSU. | • Install PSU first (bottom‑mounted or rear‑mounted).
• Mount standoffs for motherboard. | | 13 | **Install the Motherboard** | Securely mount it inside the case. | • Align I/O shield with case cut‑out.
• Tighten screws evenly. | | 14 | **Mount the CPU** | Handle with care. | • Open CPU socket latch.
• Align CPU (triangle marker) and gently place.
• Lock latch. | | 15 | **Apply Thermal Paste** | Improves heat transfer. | • Small pea‑size amount in the center of the CPU.
• Some coolers come pre‑applied. | | 16 | **Attach the CPU Cooler** | Secure and connect fan or pump. | • Follow cooler’s manual for mounting pattern.
• Connect fan/pump to CPU fan header. | | 17 | **Insert RAM** | Slot into DIMM slots. | • Open latch, align notch, press firmly until clicks. | | 18 | **Install Storage** | Mount SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot. | • For M.2, screw into motherboard.
• For SATA, use mounting brackets and SATA cables. | | 19 | **Mount the GPU** | Insert into PCIe slot. | • Remove slot cover, align with slot, push until seated.
• Secure with screws. | | 20 | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components. | • PSU 24‑pin to motherboard.
• 8‑pin CPU power.
• PCIe power to GPU.
• SATA power to drives. | | 21 | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow and looks tidy. | • Route cables behind motherboard tray.
• Use zip ties or Velcro straps. | | 22 | **Double‑Check Connections** | Prevent shorts or power issues. | • Verify all screws tightened.
• Ensure no loose cables touching metal. | | 23 | **Close the Case** | Secure panels and prepare for boot. | • Attach side panels, front panel connectors (power button, USB, audio). | | 24 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Verify hardware detection. | • Turn on PC.
• Enter BIOS (usually DEL or F2).
• Check CPU, RAM, storage, GPU status.
• Set boot priority to your OS drive. | | 25 | **Install Operating System** | Get your PC ready for use. | • Create bootable USB (Windows 10/11, Ubuntu, etc.).
• Follow on‑screen prompts. | | 26 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure optimal performance. | • Install motherboard chipset drivers.
• GPU drivers from NVIDIA/AMD.
• Update BIOS if needed. | | 27 | **Test & Benchmark** | Confirm stability. | • Run stress tests (Prime95, AIDA64, 3DMark).
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | | 28 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep your system running smoothly. | • Clean dust filters quarterly.
• Update drivers regularly.
• Monitor temperatures during heavy use. | --- #### Quick Checklist (Printable) ``` [ ] Case [ ] PSU [ ] Motherboard [ ] CPU [ ] CPU Cooler [ ] RAM [ ] Storage (SSD/HDD) [ ] GPU [ ] Case Fans [ ] Cable Management Supplies [ ] Tools (screwdriver, anti‑static strap) ``` #### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Shorted components** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; keep screws away from motherboard. | | **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow; install additional case fans. | | **Boot failure** | Double‑check CPU socket orientation; reseat RAM and GPU. | | **Power issues** | Verify PSU wattage; ensure all connectors are fully seated. | | **BIOS not detecting GPU** | Update BIOS; check PCIe slot compatibility. | --- ### Final Thought Building a PC is as rewarding as it is practical. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process of turning parts into a powerful machine tailored to your needs. Happy building!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No need to fetch recipe. Just give instructions.
